correctness.rationale: The Rayleigh minimum is concave under independent rate averaging. Exact core/leaf spectral blocks give the smallest positive eigenvalue, and strict scalar convexity yields a unique two-rate optimum and value. A two-dimensional Fourier Fiedler eigenspace forces every independent spoke rate and rim rate in the cyclic case. The cost crossover and fixed-price n-asymptotics follow by direct expansion. Exact rational and independent finite matrix checks passed, without being used as infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general-purpose SDP covers the problem as an instance but does not state or imply a closed optimal solution without solving the instance. The interconnected-network optimization holds its intra-layer graph fixed, whereas the present theorem jointly allocates all base and pendant edge rates under their relative prices. Weighted corona spectral identities alone do not solve that maximin allocation.

value.rationale: The solved object is a natural graph family comprising all vertex- and edge-transitive cores, with every edge rate independent and two physically motivated prices. Beyond a general SDP, the theorem gives one formula and explicit investable rates for all budgets and core sizes, and proves unusual all-nonuniform uniqueness on every cycle. The two investment scales and exact price crossover are structurally informative; no paper-sized extension is assumed.
